MINUTES
  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE
  NOVEMBER 12, 2020

1.  CHAIR ZERUNYAN called the meeting to order at 6:00 pm.

2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  Zerunyan, Combs, Lum, Martin, Munday,
  Pope, Vanden Bos

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Boothe, Scott

  STAFF PRESENT:  David Wahba, Director of Community Development & Public Works
  Joanne Itagaki, Traffic Engineering Deputy
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF TRAFFIC & SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES, AUGUST 18,
  2020.

COMMITTEE MEMBER VANDEN BOS made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
MUNDAY to,

  APPROVE THE TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF
  AUGUST 18, 2020.

There being no objection, CHAIR ZERUNYAN so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

NONE.

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  ROLLING HILLS ROAD BIKE LANES FINAL CONCEPT

Director Wahba stated that due to notices being received in the mail late, several members of the
public submitted comments after the August Traffic and Safety meeting. There was a request for
left hand turn lanes into the respective neighborhoods as you are travelling up or down the hill to
allow vehicles to pull out of traffic. Another item to consider is whether to add pedestrian paths on
both sides of the street. The idea is to try to improve the safety of the road, install rolled curbs and
gutters for improved drainage, add bike lanes on both sides, a pedestrian path, slightly realigning
the street and minimizing retaining walls. The objective is to have a conceptual design that the
city council can support and use it to apply for various grants for roadway improvements.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki presented the exhibits attached to the staff report. Exhibit A,
was presented with changes discussed at the last meeting; bike and pedestrian pathways were
added on the westside of Rolling Hills Road from Lariat Lane to Palos Verdes Drive North. North
of Lariat Lane, the pedestrian pathway was moved farther off the curb of the street. This was
intended to accommodate trees along the westside of the street. Trees, retaining walls, and curb
radii were considered when preparing the conceptual design.

A request was received by staff for left turn lanes to allow for vehicles to pull out from traffic. There
was concern with this due to the close proximity of the streets and driveways from each other.
This would require the widening of the street and from a cost perspective, it was determined that
this design could not move forward.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that a realignment of Rolling Hills Road was considered
and a preliminary conceptual plan was developed, Exhibit B. The realignment was considered to
try to minimize the need for retaining walls. However, there were limitations to using this design
based on roadway design requirements, public right-of-way and cost savings. These issues can
be addressed in the design of the project.

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  1
Minutes, November 12, 2020
 Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that in Exhibit A, there was discussion of installing
retaining walls in front of the South Coast Botanic Gardens, but there may be a possibility to
recompact the slopes, however, there may be steeper sections that may require retaining walls.

Traffic Engineering Deputy stated that some final thoughts are that the best opportunities for grant
funding would include bike lane connections between agencies; the pedestrian pathway could be
removed on the east side of Rolling Hills Road from Rolling Hills Road (private) to the north city
limits in order to avoid the retaining walls; in regards to the in-roadway warning lights at Rolling
Hills Road (private), other traffic controls could be explored.

Ms. Trimingham, Resident, expressed concern with plans showing the retaining walls since this
was not preferred at the last meeting; at the last meeting there was discussion of moving the
pedestrian and bike lane to the west side of the street; accommodations for the public school
buses that run on Rolling Hills Road were not included; and, she pointed out that across from
Shadow Lane there are large gas outlets from the botanical gardens that may be an issue for
construction.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that the intent was to keep the bike lanes on both sides
of Rolling Hills Road, but there is a question of whether to keep the pedestrian pathway on the
eastside of the street from Rolling Hills Road (private) to the north.

Ms. Trimingham inquired about the transition for the bike lane from Rolling Hills Road to Torrance.
Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that Torrance may have future plans to connect to the
bike lane. Director Wahba confirmed that there is a desire to do this. Traffic Engineering Deputy
Itagaki stated that when applying for grants, it is helpful to show that the two agencies are working
together.

CHAIR ZERUNYAN stated that the new city manager of Torrance understands the importance of
collaborating with neighboring jurisdictions to accomplish these tasks.

COMMITTEE MEMBER VANDEN BOS asked about the width of the current roadway and stated
that it seems with the proposed rolled curb makes the road narrower. Traffic Engineering Deputy
Itagaki stated that the existing roadway width is 24 ft. wide; adding the bike lane, will make it 36
ft. wide.

COMMITTEE MEMBER VANDEN BOS asked about a deceleration right hand turn lane on one
of the streets. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that would impact the right-of-way and
might not be possible but during design it can be considered.

Vern, Resident, expressed his concern with visibility issues. CHAIR ZERUNYAN explained that
the visibility should get better. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki confirmed that with the addition
of the bike lanes, the visibility should improve. She also suggested that if there are things
obstructing visibility, such as overgrown bushes, please call the city.

Director Wahba stated that per the comments, additional retaining walls should not be part of the
design. There was consensus that, if not feasible, removing the pedestrian pathway from the
design on the east side of the road from Palomino Lane to the Torrance city limit would be an
option.

COMMITTEE MEMBER LUM asked if pedestrians can share the equestrian trail and if so, this
would be a better option than building a retaining wall on the east side of the road. Director Wahba
stated that pedestrians and equestrians can share the trail.

COMMITTEE MEMBER LUM asked about the pathway near Rolling Hills Road. Director Wahba
stated that it is a heavily used pathway.

COMMITTEE MEMBER LUM also stated that he agreed with having a meandering pathway on
the west side of the road to save the trees.

Ms. Trimingham concurred and stated that keeping the pedestrians away from the turn lanes into
the neighborhoods is safer. Ms. Trimingham expressed her concern with the speed vehicles are
travelling near Shadow Lane.

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  2
Minutes, November 12, 2020
 COMMITTEE MEMBER VANDEN BOS made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
LUM to,

  TO KEEP THE FINAL CONCEPTUAL DESIGN AS IT IS AND THE USE OF RETAINING
  WALLS IN THE FINAL DESIGN SHOULD BE AVOIDED AS MUCH AS PRACTICAL AND
  CAN BE ACCOMMODATED BY REMOVING THE PEDESTRIAN PATHWAY ON ONE
  SIDE OF THE STREET, IF NECESSARY.

There being no objections, CHAIR ZERUNYAN so ordered.

B.  RED CURB PAINTING REQUESTS FOR FIRE HYDRANTS

Director Wahba stated that a request was received by residents in the Rollingwood Homeowner’s
Association (HOA) and Ponderosa Lanes neighborhoods to consider painting red curbs in front
of fire hydrants. The city has a policy that curbs are painted red in front of fire hydrants specifically
in commercial/business zones. Red curbs are not painted in front of fire hydrants in residential
zones. Most people know that the California Vehicle Code states that you cannot park in front of
a fire hydrant. Also, painting the curbs red takes away from the rural characteristics of the
neighborhoods. Staff contacted the Rollingwood HOA and this was discussed at one of their
meetings; there was strong opposition to painting the curbs red in front of fire hydrants.

Staff recommends that curbs in front of fire hydrants not be painted red in residential zones.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MARTIN made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
MUNDAY to,

  CONTINUE WITH POLICY OPTION A, WITH THE ADDITION TO CONTACT HOMEOWNER
  ASSOCIATIONS, WHICH STATES THE FOLLOWING:

  “Neighborhood Streets: To maintain the rural character of the City of Rolling Hills Estates,
  red curbs will not be painted for fire hydrants on neighborhood streets. This includes
  neighborhood streets with no curb, rolled curb or curb and gutter along the streets.
  Residents will be directed to request enforcement by the Sheriff’s Department.
  Recognized Howeowners Associations (HOA) will be contacted when a request is
  received from a resident on the HOA’s street.

  Business Areas: Red curbs for fire hydrants will be considered at the request of
  business/property owners on business area streets. City staff will determine if red curb is
  appropriate for the location.”

There being no objection, CHAIR ZERUNYAN so ordered.

C.  HIDDEN VALLEY ROAD AT PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH - ADDITIONAL SIGNS
  FOR TRAIL CROSSING

Director Wahba stated that there have been a couple of accidents with vehicles traveling
westbound on Palos Verdes Drive North just past Hidden Valley Road. There is an island there
that has recently been hit by a vehicle. There is a three-dot reflector at the nose of this island,
however, at night the neighbors have witnessed a couple of accidents in that section of the road.
This island nose is consistent with others along Palos Verdes Drive North and staff doesn’t see a
need to make any specific changes to address this specific traffic collision.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that staff is recommending that bike and pedestrian trail
signs be added and have them angled towards incoming traffic; post larger yield signs for users
of the pathway; and, update and relocate the existing trail signs for westbound (exiting) Hidden
Valley Road.

COMMITTEE MUNDAY asked about solutions for the island. Director Wahba stated that he and
Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki discussed adding reflectors to highlight the curve.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY stated that he has driven this area and if travelling next to a
cyclist, the curve could get a little tight.

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  3
Minutes, November 12, 2020
 Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that the nose of the island is similar to others in the area,
but the accidents may be due to the slight curve in the road.

COMMITTEE MEMBER VANDEN BOS stated that a lot of signs are installed and often ignored.
For the safety of pedestrians and better visibility for drivers, he suggested that a better solution
would be to remove the large tree, located before taking a right hand turn on Hidden Valley Road,
and flatten the dirt in that area.

CHAIR ZERUNYAN suggested pruning the tree rather than removing it and agreed with flattening
the dirt around it.

COMMITTEE MEMBER POPE agreed.

COMMITTEE MEMBER COMBS agreed and suggested removing the large rock that is in the
area.

Staff’s proposal was to 1) install two new “Bike and Pedestrian” trail crossing signs. These signs
would face the turning vehicles from Palos Verdes Drive North as they enter Hidden Valley Road;
2) remove the existing “yield” sign and replace it with a larger “yield” sign; 3) add a new yield sign
on a new post for users of the pathway; and, 4) remove the existing “bike trail” sign and replace
and relocate it with a new “bike and pedestrian trail” sign.

The COMMITTEE agreed with numbers 2 – 4 above. In regards to number 1, the COMMITTEE
agreed with the recommendation to prune the large tree that is obstructing visibility on the corner
of Palos Verdes Drive North and Hidden Valley Road and flattening the dirt around it, and later
determine whether the additional “bike and pedestrian trail” signs on this corner are necessary.

6.  COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

COMMITTEE MEMBER VANDEN BOS stated that there is a problem with the left-hand turn signal
eastbound on Palos Verdes Drive North into Hawthorne Blvd. Director Wahba stated that staff
will call the issue in to be repaired.

CHAIR ZERUNYAN thanked COMMITTEE MEMBER VANDEN BOS for all the years of
volunteering on this committee. He has served on the Palos Verdes Unified School District Board
and he and his family have been great volunteers in this city.

CHAIR ZERUNYAN thanked everyone for their service and wished everyone a Happy Holiday
Season.

7.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR ZERUNYAN adjourned the meeting at 7:08 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,  Approved by,

______________________________  _______________________________
Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant  Frank Zerunyan, Chair
